author: Reference cases for report §12.4 (handedness, parallel, antiparallel, orthogonal, oblique and zero vectors) plus tolerance-boundary and numerical-limit cases. Integer cases are derived by hand; every stored value is the output of the exact oracle tests/reference/oracles/vector-orientation-3d.ts, which shares no code with the catalogue kernel.
review: No independent human subject reviewer has approved these cases. Automated agreement is engineering evidence only.
semantics: Right-handed frame (e_x × e_y = e_z). Inputs are the exact values of IEEE-754 doubles. u·v, the components of u×v = (u_y v_z − u_z v_y, u_z v_x − u_x v_z, u_x v_y − u_y v_x) and the lengths |u|, |v|, |u×v| are exact values rounded once to the nearest double (ties to even). θ = atan2(|u×v|, u·v) ∈ [0, π] in radians; undefined (ZERO_VECTOR) when u or v is the zero vector. The unit direction of u×v is undefined (NO_CROSS_DIRECTION) exactly when u×v = 0. Relationship with τ = 1/10¹² exactly: parallel or antiparallel when |u×v|² ≤ τ²·|u|²·|v|² (by the sign of u·v), orthogonal when (u·v)² ≤ τ²·|u|²·|v|², oblique otherwise, undefined-zero-vector when a vector is zero. The angle arc is drawn exactly when u×v ≠ 0 and θ is representable; otherwise it is empty with a reason.
format: statuses and values cover every model quantity. Status "valid:UNDERFLOW" is a valid value carrying an UNDERFLOW approximation (an inexact result below the smallest normal double, or a vector with a nonzero component flushed to 0); "numerical-limit:UNDERFLOW" is a nonzero exact value that rounds to zero (value null); "undefined:<CODE>" is a mathematically undefined value (value null). Tolerances: an observed number o matches expected e when |o − e| <= absolute + relative·|e|; `exact` applies to components, dot, cross and lengths (stored as the correctly rounded double), `angle` to θ, `direction` to the unit direction of u×v. Statuses, the relationship and the arc flag always match exactly; geometry for u, v and their projections is compared exactly.
classificationTolerance: 1e-12 (the rational 1/10^12, applied to sin θ and |cos θ| through exact squared comparisons)
